notes.meaning: The Gershonite Levites were assigned to carry all the textile coverings of the tabernacle. This included the inner linen curtains, the outer layers of goat hair, ram skins, and leather, as well as the courtyard hangings and their ropes. They packed and carried all the fabric walls and roofs whenever the camp moved.

The Gershonites carried out their duties under the direct supervision of the priests. Aaron and his sons assigned each man his specific load, while Aaron's younger son, Ithamar, directly oversaw their work. This structure ensured that God's holy tent was handled with order and accountability.

Moses was commanded to count the men in the Merarite clan who were between thirty and fifty years old. This was the time of life when men had the physical strength needed for the heavy lifting of the sanctuary. Serving the Lord required their best vigor and full dedication.

The Merarites were given the heaviest transport duties of all the Levites. They carried the tabernacle's wooden frames, crossbars, pillars, and bases, along with the courtyard posts, pegs, and ropes. Moses was told to assign each item by name on a list, so that not even a single small peg was lost or neglected. Ithamar oversaw this clan just as he did the Gershonites.

Moses, Aaron, and the leaders of Israel began the census with the Kohathite clan. They registered every man from thirty to fifty years of age who was qualified to work at the Tent of Meeting. Leaders and priests worked together to carry out God's directions in an orderly way.

The census of the Kohathites showed 2,750 men who were eligible to carry out the sacred work. While their entire clan had 8,600 males from one month old and up, only this smaller group was of working age. Moses and Aaron carried out the tally strictly according to the Lord's command.

Next, the leaders counted the Gershonite clan by their families. They enrolled all the men between thirty and fifty years old who were fit to serve and carry loads. Each man counted was set apart for tabernacle duty.

The Gershonite workers totaled 2,630 men. Out of 7,500 males in the whole clan, these were the men ready to transport the curtains, coverings, and hangings. Moses and Aaron faithfully recorded everyone God had called.

The leaders then registered the Merarite men by their families. As with the other clans, the count included those between thirty and fifty years of age. They were being set apart for the demanding work of moving the tabernacle's heavy frame.

The Merarite clan had 3,200 men who were able to serve. Even though Merari was the smallest clan in total population, it had the largest number of men fit for work. God in His providence provided the most workers for the clan that carried the heaviest load.

The total number of Levites fit for service from all three clans came to 8,580 men. This matched well with the earlier total of 22,000 male Levites, showing that roughly one out of every three males was of working age. God raised up a large, well-ordered army of workers to care for His sacred dwelling.

Moses completed the registration exactly as the Lord commanded. Every single Levite received his personal task and his specific burden to carry on the march. God's people find peace and purpose when each person faithfully does the work God has assigned to them.
